pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
* GitHub is removing the underlying API used to implement the `login` command. Since the general consensus seems to be that relatively nobody currently uses this command (in favor of explicit token passing), support was simply removed for interactive login. If a future need arises, this command should be reimplemented via OAuth Device Auth Grants (eg, see https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/71628)
* login or role login commands now produce a fatal error with a descriptive message
* updated 2.10 and 2.11 porting guide entries

fixes #71560

##### SUMMARY
`ansible-galaxy login` uses the OAuth Authorizations API which is going to be deprecated on November 13, 2020. Any applications authenticating for users need to switch to their newer methods: https://docs.github.com/en/developers/apps/authorizing-oauth-apps#device-flow

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below, use your best guess if unsure -->
ansible-galaxy login

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
This affects all versions.

##### CONFIGURATION
<!--- Paste verbatim output from "ansible-config dump --only-changed" between quotes -->
```paste below

```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
<!--- Provide all relevant information below, e.g. target OS versions, network device firmware, etc. -->
This affects all environments.


##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
Everything still works today, but will fail in about 10 weeks.

There are brownout times when we should see failures to login via the CLI.

The brownouts are scheduled for:

    September 30, 2020
        From 07:00 UTC to 10:00 UTC
        From 16:00 UTC to 19:00 UTC

    October 28, 2020
        From 07:00 UTC to 10:00 UTC
        From 16:00 UTC to 19:00 UTC

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
<!--- Describe what you expected to happen when running the steps above -->
Today login works with a user's Github username and password, as long as that user has not enabled 2FA.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
On November 13 this method will no longer work and no user will be able to authenticate via Github, which is the only authentication mechanism we have for the current version of Ansible Galaxy.

This is *not* an issue we can resolve on the Galaxy side, it has to be resolved in the client.

Adding the P1 label because this will break login on all versions of the `ansible-galaxy` cli.

Backed the issue off to a P2- we don't need to create a release for this right now, but it should be dealt with as soon as reasonably possible.

Assuming the device flow works as it says, I think this won't be too big a deal to add support for. I've already got most of the code written, but the Device Flow code generation endpoint is giving me a 404 for both the real Galaxy app `client_id` as well as the test apps I've created (and opted into the Device Flow beta for). I've submitted a GitHub support ticket for that part, so hopefully it's just something dumb. Meantime, can @newswangerd or someone else with access to the Galaxy OAuth app config opt-in to the Device Flow beta so we can make sure the tokens we (eventually, hopefully) get issued are happy? Could do that for a staging Galaxy instance instead if there's one running these days, just need to know the endpoint and the `client_id` for it.

Thanks!
Glad you're taking care of this

We've not gotten any user feedback advocating for the preservation of this feature from many different channels polled, so for now we're just going to kill the feature. We'll add a descriptive error message to ansible-galaxy login that enumerates the remaining options for token auth (CLI, envvar, ~/.ansible/galaxy_token). If there's major user blowback after it's released, we can always resurrect this PR, and hopefully a future version of Galaxy can support OAuth Device Flow natively, at which point we could bring this back as an authority-agnostic option. I'll close this issue with the devel PR that kills the feature.

review_comments: Wouldn't `ansible-galaxy role -v login` be an issue here? It seems like we should just be checking if `login` was set, or maybe displaying the error in `self.execute_login`.

No worse than it was before- it'll just show the usage dump in that case with an invalid ROLE_ACTION (as it did prior to this change), since the subparser seems to require that the subcommand be first. I just didn't want to create any future trip hazards by globally blacklisting `login` as an arg value without using the parser. I tried doing this as a hidden option first, but it doesn't seem that you can do hidden subparsers in argparse. :(

What if we were to keep the code here the same but move the error to `execute_login`. That way we are still relying on argparse to resolve the args like it does today and we don't have to complicate this already complicated bit of code.
